bib.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Pretrained Foundation Models: A History from BERT to ChatGPT

question: What are the pretrained foundation models (PFMs) in text, image, graph and other modalities, how are they pretrained, and what challenges remain?
contributions: A review of PFM development in NLP, CV and GL, with insights on generalised PFM design and pretraining methodology across the three.
A summary of PFMs for speech and video, and of advanced topics: unified PFMs, efficiency and compression, security and privacy.
A discussion of challenges and opportunities for very large models, aimed at collaborative and interactive intelligence.

results.claim: The authors expect a big convergence of text, image, graph and multimodal pretraining; no unified PFM then included graphs.

limits: Pure literature review: no experiments, no comparison table of benchmark scores, so no claim of the form 'model A beats B' is backed by data here.
Cutoff is early 2023 (GPT-4, SAM, LLaMA-era); the open-weight LLM boom, DPO-style preference methods and scaling-law details are absent or only named.
ChatGPT/RLHF pipeline is described from the InstructGPT description with no numbers; Fig 5 is the only detail.

Some details look loose: BERT-base given as about 108M parameters; Sec 3.4 says compression makes performance 'deteriorate sharply' without citation; Table 1 labels some models inconsistently (e.g. MT-NLG and T0 as Contextual/MLM, Chinchilla listed as arXiv 2022).
Authors concede there is little theory for SSL, no graph PFM yet in unified models, and consistent upstream-to-downstream results are an open challenge.
practices: Pretrain on large unlabelled data with a self-supervised objective, then fine-tune or prompt for downstream tasks (Sec 1.1, 2.3).
For text generation prefer autoregressive/decoder models; for understanding prefer bidirectional encoders; BART-style encoder-decoder mixes both (Sec 3.1-3.2).
Align an LM in three steps: SFT on prompt/output pairs, train a reward model from ranked outputs, optimise with PPO (Sec 3.4-3.5, Fig 5).
Use chain-of-thought prompting for multi-step reasoning; it works better in larger models (Sec 3.5).
Use compression (pruning, quantisation, low-rank, sharing, distillation) to cut cost of PFMs (Sec 7.2).
Treat memorisation and adversarial/backdoor risk as lifecycle concerns, from data processing to deployment (Sec 7.3).

terms.definition: A model trained on large-scale data that provides a reasonable parameter initialization for a wide range of downstream applications.
A unified model pretrained on unimodal and multimodal data with single or multiple transformers as the backbone, able to perform a large variety of downstream unimodal and multimodal tasks.
Unified PFMs with one large transformer, several transformers, or a combination of both as backbone.
Three branches of word representation: next-word prediction from preceding words, prediction from both sides, and prediction over permutations of the sequence.
Erases some words randomly in the input sequence and predicts them during pretraining.
Adds noise to the corpus and reconstructs the original input.
Determines whether the LM has replaced the current token.
Uses two contiguous fragments as positives and swapped order as negatives.
A predefined task created for encoder networks to solve in pretraining, with pseudo labels generated from the data.
Two-stream SSL encoders with similar but different parameters, versus identical architectures and parameters.
